title: Sections on a zero-dimensional scheme are the product of the geometric stalks
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $C$ a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with $\dim C\le0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For each point $c\in|C|$ choose a geometric point $\bar c:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_c\to C$ lying over $c$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Then $|C|$ is finite, and for every abelian sheaf $F$ on $C_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] the map
$$\gamma_{C,F}:F(C)\longrightarrow\prod_{c\in|C|}F_{\bar c},\qquad a\longmapsto(a_{\bar c})_{c},$$
sending a global section to its germs at the pointed etale neighbourhoods $(C,\bar c)$ (stalks of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]), is an isomorphism of abelian groups, natural in $F$. (This names the map of the degree-$0$ identification in lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 03QO (lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian): for a strictly henselian local ring $R$, $\Gamma(\Spec R,\mathcal F)=\mathcal F_{\bar s}$; applied to the local Artinian pieces $\Spec\mathcal O_{C,c}$ (algebra.tex Lemma Tag 00KH: a Noetherian ring of dimension 0 is Artinian, a finite product of local Artinian rings; Section Tag 04GE, an Artinian local ring is complete hence henselian, Lemma Tag 04GM; residue field $k$ by the Nullstellensatz), with the sheaf axiom for the finite Zariski cover by disjoint open points

proof.text: *The points and their open pieces.* By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-base-change-points] (1) (with $k'=k$; its hypotheses are ours), $|C|$ is a finite discrete space and every $c\in|C|$ is a closed point with residue field $\kappa(c)=k$ [def-weil-residue-field]. So for each $c$ the set $\{c\}$ is open and closed; let $C_c\subset C$ be the open subscheme on $\{c\}$ and $j_c:C_c\to C$ its inclusion, an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. *$C_c$ is the spectrum of a local ring with one prime and residue field $k$:* choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\ni c$ of $C$ [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; $\{c\}=\{c\}\cap U$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}A$, so it contains a basic open $D(f)\ni c$, whence $D(f)=\{c\}$ and $C_c=D(f)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_f$. Put $A_c=A_f$: it has exactly one prime ideal $\mathfrak m_c$ (the prime of $c$), which is therefore its unique maximal ideal, so $A_c$ is a local ring whose only prime is $\mathfrak m_c$ (of dimension $0$), with residue field $A_c/\mathfrak m_c=\kappa(c)=k$. (One has $A_c=(A_c)_{\mathfrak m_c}=\mathcal O_{C,c}$, which is not needed.) The $C_c$, $c\in|C|$, are pairwise disjoint and cover $C$. If $C=\emptyset$ everything below holds with empty index set.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00KH (lemma-Noetherian-dimension-0), via lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-base-change-points; the basic open D(f) inside an open point is the definition of the Zariski topology on Spec A (Section Tag 00DY)

proof.text: *Each $A_c$ is strictly henselian.* $k$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure]: every nonconstant polynomial over $k$, in particular every nonconstant separable one, has a root in $k$, so $k$ is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed]. By step 1, $A_c$ is a local ring whose only prime ideal is $\mathfrak m_c$ and whose residue field $k$ is separably closed; by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-zero-local-strictly-henselian], $A_c$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

proof.text: *Sheaf condition for the disjoint cover: $F(C)\cong\prod_cF(C_c)$.* Each $j_c$ is an open immersion, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), so $(C_c,j_c)$ is an object of $C_{\Et}$ and $\{j_c:C_c\to C\}_{c\in|C|}$ is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms, i.e. a covering in $C_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For open subschemes the fibre product $C_c\times_CC_{c'}$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is the intersection $C_c\cap C_{c'}$: it is $C_c$ (with both projections the identity) for $c=c'$ and the empty scheme $\emptyset$ for $c\ne c'$. The empty family is a covering of $\emptyset$ (it is jointly surjective), so the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] for it says $F(\emptyset)$ is the equalizer of two maps between empty products, i.e. $F(\emptyset)=0$. The sheaf condition for $\{C_c\to C\}$ says $F(C)\to\prod_cF(C_c)$, $a\mapsto(a|_{C_c})_c$, is injective with image the families $(b_c)$ whose two restrictions to every $C_c\times_CC_{c'}$ agree; for $c\ne c'$ both lie in $F(\emptyset)=0$, and for $c=c'$ both are $b_c$ (restriction along the identity). Hence every family is compatible and $r_F:F(C)\to\prod_{c}F(C_c)$, $a\mapsto(a|_{C_c})_c$, is an isomorphism; it is natural in $F$ since a morphism of sheaves commutes with restrictions.

proof.text: *Sections of each piece are the stalk: $F(C_c)\cong F_{\bar c}$ through germs.* Fix $c$. Since the image $c$ of $\bar c$ lies in the open $C_c$, $\bar c$ factors uniquely as $\bar c=j_c\circ\bar c_c$ with $\bar c_c:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_c\to C_c$ [def-weil-open-immersion], a geometric point of $C_c=\operatorname{Spec}A_c$ lying over its closed point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $G_c=F|_{C_c}$, $G_c(V\to C_c)=F(V\to C_c\xrightarrow{j_c}C)$, an abelian sheaf on $(C_c)_{\Et}$ with $G_c(C_c)=F(C_c)$, and $\rho_F:j_c^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}G_c$ the natural isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1) ($j_c$ is etale, step 3). (a) By step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] applied to $R=A_c$, $\bar s=\bar c_c$, the germ map $\sigma_c:G_c(C_c)\to(G_c)_{\bar c_c}$ is an isomorphism, natural in $F$. (b) Let $\theta_c=c_{j_c,\bar c_c,F}\circ(\rho_{F,\bar c_c})^{-1}:(G_c)_{\bar c_c}\to F_{\bar c}$, where $\rho_{F,\bar c_c}:(j_c^{-1}F)_{\bar c_c}\to(G_c)_{\bar c_c}$ is the isomorphism induced on stalks by the sheaf isomorphism $\rho_F$ (it sends the germ of $x$ at $(V,\bar v)$ to the germ of $\rho_F(V)(x)$ there, by the colimit definition of stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]) and $c_{j_c,\bar c_c,F}:(j_c^{-1}F)_{\bar c_c}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{j_c\circ\bar c_c}=F_{\bar c}$ is the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]; $\theta_c$ is an isomorphism, natural in $F$. (c) *Germ compatibility:* for $b\in F(C_c)=G_c(C_c)$, $\theta_c(\sigma_c(b))$ is the germ of $b$ at the pointed etale neighbourhood $(C_c,\bar c_c)$ of $\bar c$ in $C_{\Et}$. Indeed, $j_c$ is a monomorphism, so the projection $p:C_c\times_CC_c\to C_c$ is an isomorphism and a morphism of pointed etale neighbourhoods $(C_c\times_CC_c,(\bar c_c,\bar c_c))\to(C_c,\bar c_c)$ of $\bar c_c$ in $(C_c)_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (2) with $W=C_c$, $\rho_F(C_c\times_CC_c)(\eta_{j_c,F}(C_c)(b))=p^*b$, whose germ at $(C_c\times_CC_c,(\bar c_c,\bar c_c))$ equals the germ of $b$ at $(C_c,\bar c_c)$, i.e. $\sigma_c(b)$; so $(\rho_{F,\bar c_c})^{-1}\sigma_c(b)$ is the germ of $\eta_{j_c,F}(C_c)(b)$ at $(C_c\times_CC_c,(\bar c_c,\bar c_c))$, which $c_{j_c,\bar c_c,F}$ sends to the germ of $b$ at $(C_c,\bar c_c)$ by the germ compatibility of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] (with $U=C_c$, $\bar u=\bar c_c$). Hence $g_c=\theta_c\circ\sigma_c:F(C_c)\to F_{\bar c}$, $b\mapsto$ (germ of $b$ at $(C_c,\bar c_c)$), is an isomorphism, natural in $F$.

proof.text: *The map $\gamma_{C,F}$ is the composite, hence an isomorphism, natural in $F$.* For $a\in F(C)$ and $c\in|C|$, $j_c:(C_c,\bar c_c)\to(C,\bar c)$ is a morphism of pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar c$ ($j_c\circ\bar c_c=\bar c$), so by the definition of the stalk as a colimit [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] the germ of $a$ at $(C,\bar c)$ equals the germ of $a|_{C_c}$ at $(C_c,\bar c_c)$: $a_{\bar c}=g_c(a|_{C_c})$ (step 4). Hence $\gamma_{C,F}=\bigl(\prod_cg_c\bigr)\circ r_F$ with $r_F$ the isomorphism of step 3 and each $g_c$ an isomorphism (step 4): $\gamma_{C,F}$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Naturality: for a morphism $\varphi:F\to F'$ of abelian sheaves, $\varphi$ commutes with restriction maps, hence with the colimit maps to the stalks, so $\gamma_{C,F'}\circ\varphi(C)=\bigl(\prod_c\varphi_{\bar c}\bigr)\circ\gamma_{C,F}$. Finiteness of $|C|$ is step 1.
